{
  "technical_and_design_decisions": [
    "Use the existing Spring XD module and build conventions rather than introducing a new module framework.",
    "Implement the Kafka load-generator source as a configurable source module with topic, partition, message-size, rate, and offset-related properties exposed through the existing configuration model.",
    "Implement the load-receiving sink as a streaming sink that counts received records and bytes and exposes throughput measurements through logs and/or the existing metrics mechanism.",
    "Use an EC2 Linux AMI with Java 17+, Kafka client/runtime dependencies, build tools, and performance-test scripts preinstalled; keep the AMI creation reproducible through an image-build script or documented provisioning process.",
    "Use the existing CI provider and Windows worker/image mechanism, adding scheduled builds and preserving test diagnostics rather than attempting to redesign the CI system.",
    "Correct Kafka source offset handling using explicit offset assignment and seek behavior, with tests covering initial offsets, partition-specific offsets, restart behavior, and offset boundaries.",
    "Measure simple-stream performance using a repeatable source-to-sink benchmark, fixed message sizes, controlled duration, warm-up, and throughput reporting.",
    "Publish static GitHub Pages content generated from repository documentation and examples, organized into samples, tutorials, links, performance benchmarks, and reference architectures.",
    "Treat the Lattice/Diego work as a time-boxed proof of concept for a pluggable runtime SPI, documenting lifecycle, deployment, networking, resource, and failure-handling implications without committing to production integration.",
    "Use automated unit, integration, and smoke tests where practical, with manual validation for cloud-image, Windows-CI, and Lattice/Diego environments."
  ],
  "assumptions": [
    "The existing repository, build, Kafka integration, Spring XD runtime, and CI infrastructure are available and can be modified by one developer.",
    "The increment targets Java 17 or later and uses the repository's current supported Spring and Kafka versions.",
    "The source and sink modules are new modules within the existing project and do not require a new public protocol or external service.",
    "Kafka brokers and test infrastructure can be provisioned or accessed for integration and performance testing; broker development and production operations are out of scope.",
    "The EC2 AMI is intended for development and performance testing, not production hardening, compliance certification, or multi-region deployment.",
    "Windows CI scheduling includes configuration, image/worker experimentation, diagnostics, and isolation of remaining failures; fixing every pre-existing test failure is out of scope.",
    "Performance testing covers one representative simple stream and produces baseline throughput numbers rather than a comprehensive benchmark matrix.",
    "The GitHub Pages site is a static site with modest navigation and styling; custom backend services, authentication, and extensive content authoring are out of scope.",
    "The Lattice/Diego POC can use mocked or locally simulated components where a full deployment environment is unavailable.",
    "Effort includes implementation, code review preparation, automated tests, documentation, and developer verification, but excludes waiting time for external infrastructure or approvals.",
    "Estimates are most likely single-developer work-hour estimates and do not represent elapsed calendar duration."
  ],
  "activities": [
    {
      "activity_id": "A1",
      "activity_name": "Increment analysis and implementation planning",
      "activity_description": "Inspect the existing Spring XD architecture, module conventions, Kafka integration, build system, CI configuration, documentation structure, and relevant runtime extension points; refine the implementation plan and acceptance checks for all eight user stories.",
      "most_likely_effort": 16
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A2",
      "activity_name": "EC2 AMI for Kafka performance tests",
      "activity_description": "Define the AMI contents, provision Java, Kafka and required client/build packages, add reproducible provisioning or image-build automation, configure performance-test utilities, create the image, and validate that a Kafka performance test can run from it.",
      "most_likely_effort": 32
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A3",
      "activity_name": "Kafka load-generator source module",
      "activity_description": "Design and implement the source module, configuration properties, Kafka producer integration, message generation and rate controls, lifecycle behavior, error handling, documentation, unit tests, and an integration smoke test.",
      "most_likely_effort": 56
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A4",
      "activity_name": "Load-receiving sink module",
      "activity_description": "Design and implement the sink module, consume incoming records, count records and bytes, calculate and report received throughput, expose configuration and metrics consistent with the existing runtime, and add tests and usage documentation.",
      "most_likely_effort": 48
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A5",
      "activity_name": "Windows scheduled CI builds",
      "activity_description": "Configure scheduled Windows builds, select or experiment with suitable Windows AMI/worker images, capture and classify test failures, isolate environment-specific failures, update scripts or dependencies as needed, and document the remaining failures and infrastructure requirements.",
      "most_likely_effort": 48
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A6",
      "activity_name": "Kafka source offset-management correction",
      "activity_description": "Trace the existing Kafka source offset behavior, implement correct offset assignment, seeking, and fetch semantics, handle partition and restart cases, add regression and integration tests, and update configuration or operational documentation.",
      "most_likely_effort": 40
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A7",
      "activity_name": "Simple-stream performance characterization",
      "activity_description": "Build a repeatable source-to-sink performance scenario, define measurement methodology and warm-up behavior, execute controlled runs, collect throughput and relevant runtime metrics, analyze results, and record baseline performance numbers and limitations.",
      "most_likely_effort": 32
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A8",
      "activity_name": "Static GitHub Pages collateral site",
      "activity_description": "Select or configure a static-site structure, organize samples, tutorials, links, performance benchmarks, and reference architectures, add navigation and basic styling, configure GitHub Pages publication, and verify links and rendered content.",
      "most_likely_effort": 40
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A9",
      "activity_name": "Lattice/Diego pluggable-runtime SPI proof of concept",
      "activity_description": "Investigate Lattice/Diego integration points, define a candidate runtime SPI and lifecycle model, implement a minimal demonstrator or adapter, exercise deployment and failure scenarios where possible, identify risks and constraints, and document scope, architecture options, and follow-up work.",
      "most_likely_effort": 96
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A10",
      "activity_name": "Cross-feature integration, regression testing, and delivery",
      "activity_description": "Run the relevant build and test suites, perform integration checks across the new Kafka modules and performance environment, resolve increment-related defects, review configuration and documentation, and prepare the final deliverable and change summary.",
      "most_likely_effort": 32
    }
  ],
  "reported_total": {
    "most_likely_effort": 440
  }
}

technical_and_design_decisions: Use the existing Spring XD module and build conventions rather than introducing a new module framework.
Implement the Kafka load-generator source as a configurable source module with topic, partition, message-size, rate, and offset-related properties exposed through the existing configuration model.
Implement the load-receiving sink as a streaming sink that counts received records and bytes and exposes throughput measurements through logs and/or the existing metrics mechanism.

Use an EC2 Linux AMI with Java 17+, Kafka client/runtime dependencies, build tools, and performance-test scripts preinstalled; keep the AMI creation reproducible through an image-build script or documented provisioning process.
Use the existing CI provider and Windows worker/image mechanism, adding scheduled builds and preserving test diagnostics rather than attempting to redesign the CI system.
Correct Kafka source offset handling using explicit offset assignment and seek behavior, with tests covering initial offsets, partition-specific offsets, restart behavior, and offset boundaries.
Measure simple-stream performance using a repeatable source-to-sink benchmark, fixed message sizes, controlled duration, warm-up, and throughput reporting.
Publish static GitHub Pages content generated from repository documentation and examples, organized into samples, tutorials, links, performance benchmarks, and reference architectures.

Treat the Lattice/Diego work as a time-boxed proof of concept for a pluggable runtime SPI, documenting lifecycle, deployment, networking, resource, and failure-handling implications without committing to production integration.
Use automated unit, integration, and smoke tests where practical, with manual validation for cloud-image, Windows-CI, and Lattice/Diego environments.
assumptions: The existing repository, build, Kafka integration, Spring XD runtime, and CI infrastructure are available and can be modified by one developer.
The increment targets Java 17 or later and uses the repository's current supported Spring and Kafka versions.
The source and sink modules are new modules within the existing project and do not require a new public protocol or external service.
Kafka brokers and test infrastructure can be provisioned or accessed for integration and performance testing; broker development and production operations are out of scope.
The EC2 AMI is intended for development and performance testing, not production hardening, compliance certification, or multi-region deployment.
Windows CI scheduling includes configuration, image/worker experimentation, diagnostics, and isolation of remaining failures; fixing every pre-existing test failure is out of scope.
Performance testing covers one representative simple stream and produces baseline throughput numbers rather than a comprehensive benchmark matrix.
The GitHub Pages site is a static site with modest navigation and styling; custom backend services, authentication, and extensive content authoring are out of scope.
The Lattice/Diego POC can use mocked or locally simulated components where a full deployment environment is unavailable.
Effort includes implementation, code review preparation, automated tests, documentation, and developer verification, but excludes waiting time for external infrastructure or approvals.
Estimates are most likely single-developer work-hour estimates and do not represent elapsed calendar duration.

activities.activity_description: Inspect the existing Spring XD architecture, module conventions, Kafka integration, build system, CI configuration, documentation structure, and relevant runtime extension points; refine the implementation plan and acceptance checks for all eight user stories.

activities.activity_name: EC2 AMI for Kafka performance tests
activities.activity_description: Define the AMI contents, provision Java, Kafka and required client/build packages, add reproducible provisioning or image-build automation, configure performance-test utilities, create the image, and validate that a Kafka performance test can run from it.

Design and implement the source module, configuration properties, Kafka producer integration, message generation and rate controls, lifecycle behavior, error handling, documentation, unit tests, and an integration smoke test.

Design and implement the sink module, consume incoming records, count records and bytes, calculate and report received throughput, expose configuration and metrics consistent with the existing runtime, and add tests and usage documentation.

Configure scheduled Windows builds, select or experiment with suitable Windows AMI/worker images, capture and classify test failures, isolate environment-specific failures, update scripts or dependencies as needed, and document the remaining failures and infrastructure requirements.

Trace the existing Kafka source offset behavior, implement correct offset assignment, seeking, and fetch semantics, handle partition and restart cases, add regression and integration tests, and update configuration or operational documentation.

Build a repeatable source-to-sink performance scenario, define measurement methodology and warm-up behavior, execute controlled runs, collect throughput and relevant runtime metrics, analyze results, and record baseline performance numbers and limitations.

Select or configure a static-site structure, organize samples, tutorials, links, performance benchmarks, and reference architectures, add navigation and basic styling, configure GitHub Pages publication, and verify links and rendered content.

activities.activity_name: Lattice/Diego pluggable-runtime SPI proof of concept
activities.activity_description: Investigate Lattice/Diego integration points, define a candidate runtime SPI and lifecycle model, implement a minimal demonstrator or adapter, exercise deployment and failure scenarios where possible, identify risks and constraints, and document scope, architecture options, and follow-up work.

activities.activity_name: Cross-feature integration, regression testing, and delivery
activities.activity_description: Run the relevant build and test suites, perform integration checks across the new Kafka modules and performance environment, resolve increment-related defects, review configuration and documentation, and prepare the final deliverable and change summary.
